precepts.text: Before Zerubbabel the great mountain, Babylon, becomes a plain, and he shall bring forth the headstone with shoutings of grace, grace unto it; Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, and Zerubbabel is of Solomon's line.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. Who is that, brothers? That is Christ; he is the headstone.
precepts.point: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it. His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. However, this goes deeper than that: verses 6 through 9 are also going into the last days.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.

precepts.text: And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord. Watch what he calls Babylon: Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain. And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever. That right there lets you know it is not Iraq: are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says thou shalt be desolate for ever; so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.
precepts.point: Who art thou, O great mountain? Remember, Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity; Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So this great mountain is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Does everybody understand that?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Zechariah asks, “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”. Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity, and Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So who is this great mountain? Jeremiah shows where the mountain is: “And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.”

Watch what he calls Babylon: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.” The great mountain is Babylon.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.” That lets you know it is not Iraq. Are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says “thou shalt be desolate for ever”, so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.

So the great mountain before Zerubbabel is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Before him it becomes a plain, flattened and destroyed, and it is done “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills.

precepts.text: In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan: the language of Canaan is referring to the scriptures. In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt: it is talking about where the Israelites are, here in Babylon the great, the spiritual Egypt. And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them. Who is that saviour? Christ.
precepts.point: Who art thou, O great mountain? Remember, Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity; Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So this great mountain is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Does everybody understand that?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

precepts.text: These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.
precepts.point: I will give power unto my two witnesses. Before every judgment God sends two prophets: Isaiah and Jeremiah, Joshua and Zerubbabel, Moses and Elijah.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof?” Zechariah asks again about “these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves.” The oil is understanding. The answer: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”

The two anointed ones are the two witnesses. In Zechariah’s time they were Joshua the priest and Zerubbabel. Before Babylon it was Isaiah and Jeremiah; in Revelation 11 it is Moses and Elijah. Different names, different people, but the same pattern: God always sends his prophets forth in twos before he brings forth judgment.

That is why Christ sent the twelve and the seventy elders out two by two. You cannot make judgment without two witnesses. And when the witnesses come they bind and loose things on earth, they forgive and they condemn, because it is the Lord speaking through them.

The two witnesses also speak of Israel as a whole. God says his people are his witnesses; and there are the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the northern and southern kingdom. A witness has a testimony, and Israel is sent to testify on this earth before the judgment comes.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts; the only way Israel overcomes.
precepts.point: David understood he did not need the sword, the spear, or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
When the Philistine saw David, “he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.” “Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves?” He cursed David by his gods and promised to give his flesh “unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.”

David answered, “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.” Again the record shows who the army of the Most High is: Israel.

David understood he did not need the sword, the spear or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” That is the only way Israel overcomes. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
precepts.point: Israel's forefathers died only when the Most High said it was time; that is the only way any of them died. David mourned Jonathan, saying his love to him was wonderful, passing the love of women.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.”

David “bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow”, and his lament is “written in the book of Jasher.” The book of Jasher is not in the canon because the Most High did not will us to have it; he put in the book exactly what he wanted his people to read in the last days.

And the bow is not how this walk goes in the last days. It is not by might nor by power, but by the Spirit of the Lord. The captivity is not overthrown by rising up with the bow or the gun; this is spiritual war and not physical. There is nothing wrong with knowing how to defend yourself, but the redemption of Israel does not come by force of arms.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by the spirit of the Most High, for the battle is His to fight for His people.
precepts.point: Sennacherib departs and dwells at Nineveh, and as he worships in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smite him with the sword and flee, and Esarhaddon his son reigns in his stead, fulfilling the word of verse 7.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.”

Israel did not lift a finger: “the angel of the Lord went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand.” A score is twenty, so that is a hundred and eighty-five thousand, all dead corpses by morning.

The battle is the Most High’s to fight for his people. This is praying for the death of the enemy and for righteous judgment, and leaving it to his spirit, not to might or power.

precepts.text: Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, saith the Lord of hosts; these things, the destroying of the nations, will be by the Lord's Spirit.
precepts.point: I will greatly praise the Lord with my mouth and praise Him among the multitude, for He shall stand at the right hand of the poor, the Israelites, to save him from those that condemn his soul. He saves the poor by His commandments; keeping God's commandments and enduring in this truth is how we will be saved.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“That they may know that this is thy hand; that thou, Lord, hast done it.” The adversaries will know it was the Lord, because “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.”

These things, the destroying of the nations, will be by the Lord's Spirit, not by our might or power. That is how they will know that this is his hand and that he has done it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why:
“And the angel that talked with me came again, and waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep, And said unto me, What seest thou? And I said, I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, with a bowl upon the top of it, and his seven lamps thereon, and seven pipes to the seven lamps, which are upon the top thereof:” He is seeing a vision of the menorah. “And two olive trees by it,” Remember Revelation 11:4 says two olive trees and two candlesticks. “one upon the right side of the bowl, and the other upon the left side thereof. So I answered and spake to the angel that talked with me, saying, What are these, my lord? Then the angel that talked with me answered and said unto me, Knowest thou not what these be? And I said, No, my lord. Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” So these two olive trees, these two candlesticks, make reference to Joshua the high priest and Zerubbabel, who was the governor. It goes into the law and the testimony, and it is also symbolic of the two kingdoms.

“Who art thou, O great mountain?” The great mountain, as we read later on, is talking about Babylon the great. “before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” The headstone is the cornerstone, making reference to Christ, who is called the BRANCH in chapter 3. He shall bring it forth with shoutings, crying grace, grace, mercy, mercy unto it. “Moreover the word of the Lord came unto me, saying, The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it; and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the Lord, which run to and fro through the whole earth.” The plummet is the measuring line. Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the building of the temple, and his hands would also finish it, which he did; when he rebuilt the temple they said it didn't compare to the glory of the original one Solomon built. This is a twofold chapter; it is also going into the last days, but that is for another lesson.

“Then answered I, and said unto him, What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof? And I answered again, and said unto him, What be these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves?” The golden oil is going into the wisdom and knowledge of God. Notice the same analogy is given in Revelation about the two olive trees and the two candlesticks; that is why it is twofold. “And he answered me and said, Knowest thou not what these be? And I said, No, my lord. Then said he, These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.” So the two olive trees and the two candlesticks, when you follow the precepts with Joshua and Zerubbabel, actually represent the two kingdoms, and they also represent the law and the testimony.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
Zechariah prophesies about Zerubbabel in the last days; he prophesies about Israel being raised up, Christ being raised up. “Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do is going to be by the spirit of the Lord; it is not by might nor by our own power, but by the spirit of the Lord.

“Who art thou, O great mountain?” This is talking about the same mountain, the great mountain of Revelation 8:8. “before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain:” Letting you know Zerubbabel is going to be around in the last days. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof” The headstone is Christ, because Christ comes out of that lineage of Judah. “with shoutings,” Shoutings are prayers. “crying, Grace, grace unto it.” We are going to be crying grace, grace unto it, unto the Lord.
